A trick that seems to work is to set the left edge at 0, which on a log
scale will be transformed to -Inf

Here is an example using the mtcars data, and drawing a line to the
left-most point:

# get a set of target points, one for each line
start_points <- ddply(mtcars, .(cyl), function(DF) {
   DF[DF$wt == min(DF$wt),]
})

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg, colour=factor(cyl))) +
   geom_point() +
   geom_line() +
   geom_segment(data=start_points, aes(xend = wt, y=mpg, yend=mpg), x=0) +
   scale_x_log10()

--

The following piece of code demonstrates my problem

library(ggplot2)
mydf <- data.frame(
x=rnorm(110),
f=rep(c("a","b"),c(100,10)),
wt=rep(1,110))
ggplot(aes(x=x,color=y),data=mydf)+geom_density()
ggplot(aes(x=x,color=y,weight=wt),data=mydf)+geom_density()
ggplot(aes(x=x,color=y,weight=wt/sum(wt)),data=mydf)+geom_density()

I am plotting densities for 2 groups of unequal size.
The first plot, without weights, creates densities with equal total weight for both groups.
The second and third plot do not do this.

Of course, it is possible to compute adjusted weights normalizing the sum for both groups,
but it would be better if there were a way of forcing equal total weights when plotting densities for multiple groups.
Can this be done?

messages.subject_clean: Manual scale for geom_raster
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thiago,
As with other geoms, you can use factor() in your geom_raster to get R to treat your z variable as categories. So it would be:
geom_raster(data=df, aes(x, y, fill = factor(z)))

Some things to note.

First, your random function is going to return continuous values, so they'll all be different with virtual certainty. I assume in your real implementation, you have data that more "naturally" inclines itself toward categories. If your data really are continuous, the gradient color probably is the best way to display them.

Second, when you're picking the manual colors you mentioned, bear in mind the levels in a factor are sorted alphabetically. This is how ggplot2 maps the vectors values and labels to your factor. So when assigning labels and colors (through scale_color_manual), it'll look like this:

df <- data.frame(x=1:20, y=1:20, z=c(rep('x',5), rep('z',5), rep('w',5), rep('a',5)))
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data=df, aes(x=x, y=y, color=z), shape=15,size=20) +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("red","brown","ivory","yellow"),
    labels=c("apples","walnuts","xylophones","zits"))

Hope this helps!
- Peter

d <- read.csv("pdp.csv")

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(dmelted,aes(Period,value,color=variable))+geom_line()

messages.body_plain:
Hi

I am trying to draw biplots in ggplot2, that is the type with calibrated non-orthogonal axes for more than two variables as in the attached file. This is not too hard to do, but annotating the axes is proving to be a time-wasting/deal-breaking issue.

As in the attached graph, it is usual to identify the biplot axes by placing the name of the variable at the positive end of the axis. E.g. in the attached figure, variable 'NumVes' increases towards the top right of the graph while 'RayH' increases towards the left side. In base graphics I would just do the annotations with mtext(), but there does not seem to be an easy way to do this in ggplot2. I do not want to place the variable names in the plot region - it should be in the margin.

I would really appreciate any suggestions regarding how to do this (of course with the least amount of effort). Things I have considered from other posts in the group and on Stack Overflow include the following:

Using annotation_custom() or the like to add a textGrob() with the text, which can be displayed in the margin only if clipping is disabled. (e.g. see http://stackoverflow.com/questions/12409960/ggplot2-annotate-outside-of-plot)
I could use the x- and y-axes with specified tick marks and labels, but that will only work for variables which are positive towards the left or bottom of the plot. As I have it it is not possible to add second x- ands y-axes in ggplot2 so that rules it out. (e.g. http://stackoverflow.com/a/3101876)
Using gtable and adding grobs to the rows and columns, something like in this post http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17492230/how-to-place-grobs-with-annotation-custom-at-precise-areas-of-the-plot-region/17493256#17493256.
I can do the annotations in a separate viewport and display the plotting region within a viewport added on top. This is probably doable (with alignment issues) but I would rather go for ggplot2 solutions.

None of these seem very satisfying to me. Does anyone have other suggestions regarding how to do this? This is so much easier with base graphics' mtext() but I was really hoping to leverage ggplot2 for this. This is a situation where multiple x- and y-axes would come in handy (and it would not have violate philosophical issues as the axes would not contain any actual scales).

Pieter

Tung,

There is probably a better way of doing this but how about bringing
the simulated and observed data together, then using scale_size_manual
and scale_linetype_manual to remove the points and lines you do not
want to show:

# combine observed and simulated data
all <- rbind(Obs_melt,Sim_melt)

# factor to differentiate observed and simulated (no differentiation
between individual simulations)
all$vfac <-
factor(ifelse(all$variable=="Obs","Observed","Simulated"),levels=c("Simulated","Observed"))

Sim_plot <- ggplot(data = all, aes(x = Date, y = value)) +
   geom_line(aes(group = variable,colour=vfac,linetype=vfac))+
   geom_point(aes(group=variable,size=vfac,colour=vfac))+
   scale_colour_manual(name="Legend",values=c("#999999","#0000FF"))+
   scale_size_manual(name="Legend",values=c(0,2))+ # zero size for
simulated points
   scale_linetype_manual(name="Legend",values=c(1,0)) # no linetype for
observed data

Ron.

Hi Ron,

Thanks a lot for helping! It works nicely now. I also expand your code a little bit to automatically plot different color for different simulations

# Ref: https://github.com/jennybc/STAT545A_2013/blob/master/block14_colors.rmd
library(RColorBrewer)
# get number of variables
n_q <- length(levels(all$variable))
# get color based on number of variables
display.brewer.pal(n = n_q, name = 'Dark2')
jBrewColors <- brewer.pal(n = n_q, name = "Dark2")
# number of simulation (minus observation)
n_sim <- n_q - 1
# got values for point & lines later
zero_point <- rep(0, n_sim)
one_point <- rep(1, n_sim)

all$vfac2 <- factor(all$variable)

Sim_plot <- ggplot(data = all, aes(x = Date, y = value)) +

  geom_line(aes(group = variable, colour = vfac2, linetype = vfac2))+
  geom_point(aes(group = variable, size = vfac2, colour = vfac2))+
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Legend", values = jBrewColors)+
  scale_size_manual(name = "Legend", values = c(2, zero_point))+ # zero size for simulated points
  scale_linetype_manual(name="Legend",values = c(0, one_point)) # no linetype for observed data
Sim_plot

Cheers,

Tung
